solutions.check: 29 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: An atomic variant, I thus get pissed regularly

blocks.note: taken as written
so means thus, in this way
to tope is to drink alcohol habitually

explanation.surface: A confession of drinking too often, oddly tacked onto a physics term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Regularly' looks like an alternate-letter signal, but here it is part of the meaning: to tope is to drink heavily as a habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Atoms of one element with differing neutron counts are its different forms, each called by this chemistry term.

clue.text: Breaks, as the piss artist said, for a drink?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs his words, so we hear the word as a drunk would pronounce it

blocks.note: snaps means breaks; slurred by a drunk, the s becomes sh

explanation.surface: A drunk, slurring, asks for a break to have another drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A piss artist is British slang for a heavy drinker; his slurred 'snaps' comes out with a 'sh' sound.
explanation.definitionFit: This strong clear spirit, often flavoured with fruit, is a kind of alcoholic liquor from Germany and Scandinavia.

clue.text: see 20ac.
Be a moralizing sort of chap – i.e. Fry broadcasting

indicators.note: a sort of something is a rough version of it, so the letters are reworked
broadcasting scatters things widely, so the following letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, without the dots
taken as written; Stephen Fry, the broadcaster

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry on air comes across as a sermonising sort of fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry is Stephen Fry, a British TV and radio personality, which makes 'broadcasting' blend into the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To preachify is to lecture tediously about morals, sermonising in a self-righteous manner.

clue.text: Belligerent Russian, strutting male, holding dick that's 'on the turn'

indicators.note: something on the turn is turning round, so the word is read backwards
holding means gripping something inside, so one word goes around another

blocks.note: a cock is a male bird that struts about
a dick and an ass are both slang for a fool

explanation.surface: An aggressive Russian, a strutting male, holding something that's going off.
explanation.definitionFit: Cossacks were Russian horsemen famed as fierce warriors, so a Cossack is a warlike Russian figure.

clue.text: Band taking month putting on extra tight tops

indicators.note: the tops of words are their opening letters
putting one thing on another places it right after, building a sequence

blocks.note: OCT is the calendar abbreviation for October
the first letters of extra and tight

explanation.surface: A band takes a month to squeeze into extra-tight tops.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of eight musicians playing together is a small musical band or ensemble.

clue.text: Broadcaster going under – the downfall of high fliers

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite TV broadcaster
diving is going under water

explanation.surface: A broadcaster goes bust, a fall from grace for its high-flying executives.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like a business collapse; the definition is literal: people jumping from planes fall down from a great height.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumping from an aircraft and freefalling before opening a parachute is literally a descent for those up in planes.

clue.text: Limerick about Tony desperate to rope in UKIP leader?

indicators.note: someone desperate is in a state of disorder, so the name is jumbled
the leader of a word is its first letter
to rope in is to draw something inside, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: C is short for circa, about
taken as written
the first letter of UKIP

explanation.surface: A limerick about a desperate Tony trying to recruit the UKIP leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Limerick looks like a comic poem but is the Irish county; UKIP was a British anti-EU party.
explanation.definitionFit: Limerick is an administrative region in the west of Ireland, one of that country's thirty-two counties.

clue.text: Peer aims to get in this legislative assembly corporation

definitions.text: Peer aims to get in this

blocks.note: a parliament meets in a chamber, and the house itself is called one
corporation is old slang for a big belly, as is pot

explanation.surface: A member of the Lords hopes to get into this law-making body.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Peer' as pee-er, one who pees: that is who aims for this vessel. Corporation is dated British slang for a paunch, like pot belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl kept under the bed for urinating at night is exactly the target for someone relieving himself.

clue.text: Sacked TV host's broadcast looks at "male member"

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard on air, so we go by the sound of the words

blocks.note: to peer is to look closely
M is the abbreviation for male
a member is a body part, an organ

explanation.surface: A fired TV presenter's show eyes up the male member.
explanation.walkthrough: Piers Morgan is a British TV presenter and former tabloid editor who was famously sacked from the Daily Mirror.
explanation.definitionFit: This television presenter and journalist has been dismissed from more than one job, notably as Mirror editor.

clue.text: see 14ac.
Drink set bra on fire almost

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so the letters are put in a new order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is lost

blocks.note: taken as written
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: An instruction to set a bra alight, almost, as a feminist gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On fire' wants to be read together, but 'set' and 'fire' work separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Barsac is a sweet white wine from the Bordeaux region of France, named after its commune.

clue.text: Tired out, undergoing a tense penetration, humble yourself

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are rearranged
being penetrated means having something pushed inside

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Worn out after a nervous sexual encounter, someone is told to be humble.
explanation.walkthrough: Note that 'a tense' is both the A and the T that go inside, not part of the indicator's meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat dirt is an idiom for accepting humiliation and grovelling, debasing oneself before others.

clue.text: (& 11/26) Spread our pages, readers, and accept how bad things really are!

definitions.text: accept how bad things really are

blocks.note: first meaning: Private Eye talking to its readers

blocks.clueFragment: accept how bad things really are
blocks.note: second meaning: stop ignoring the unpleasant truth

explanation.surface: A magazine urges its readers to open it up and face the grim truth.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is from Private Eye, so 'our pages' are the Eye's: readers opening the magazine would open 'your Eyes'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for facing reality, recognising unpleasant facts instead of ignoring or denying them.

clue.text: Explanations unacceptable once sex is cleaned up across America

indicators.note: cleaning up tidies things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged
lying across something means spanning it, so the letters are put around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
US is the usual abbreviation for America

explanation.surface: Once American sexual mores are cleaned up, no explanations will be accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase states that no justification will be tolerated: whatever reasons are offered, none will be accepted.

clue.text: Inability to get off when one tinkered with onanism

indicators.note: tinkering is fiddling about with something, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone can't finish while fiddling with himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get off' suggests sexual climax given the onanism, but here it means get off to sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia is chronic sleeplessness, being unable to drift into slumber at night.

clue.text: Show-ring election promises?

blocks.note: to manifest is to show
O is ring-shaped

explanation.walkthrough: Show-ring looks like an arena for animals, but splits into two pieces; the question mark flags that a party's pledges are only examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A party publishes a document of its policies before a vote, setting out what it pledges to do.

clue.text: German minister doctored Beeb's log

indicators.note: something doctored has been tampered with, so the letters are altered in order

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A government minister has falsified the BBC's records.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is the British nickname for the BBC, which makes falsified records a pointed choice: propaganda.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Goebbels was the Nazi propaganda chief, a minister in Hitler's government.

clue.text: Pissed over Sony in no time at all

indicators.note: pissed is British slang for drunk, and drunk letters stagger about

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk over a Sony gadget almost instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases describe something happening shortly, with only a brief wait before it occurs.

clue.text: (& 3dn.) Sentimentality associated with Democrat 'X' is what Osborne would love to promise

definitions.text: what Osborne would love to promise

blocks.note: goo is sickly sentimentality
D is the abbreviation for Democrat
the x symbol means multiplied by, read as times

explanation.surface: A sentimental Democrat is linked with a mysterious X, apparently an Osborne pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: George Osborne was the UK Chancellor of the Exchequer during austerity, so promising prosperity was beyond him.
explanation.definitionFit: A finance minister cutting spending would dearly like to pledge prosperity and fun ahead, a happy era.

clue.text: Feature of slob Eye derided didn't break the rules

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters sit within the words

blocks.note: found inside the run of letters across these three words

explanation.surface: A slob mocked by Private Eye nevertheless kept within the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who complied with regulations followed them, doing as instructed rather than flouting them.

clue.text: Support Clegg's no. 2? Move over, there's work still to be done!

indicators.note: number two in a name is its second letter
turning over flips a word, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to back someone is to support them
the second letter of Clegg
a go is a move or turn

explanation.surface: Back Nick Clegg's deputy and shift aside, as there's a pile of work outstanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick Clegg was Deputy Prime Minister, Britain's 'no. 2', which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: An accumulation of unfinished tasks waiting to be dealt with is a pile of arrears.

clue.text: A cow, Balls at heart, he admits?

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

blocks.note: the middle letter of Balls
an ower is one who owes, the debtor who admits he owes

explanation.surface: Ed Balls, deep down, confesses he is a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Balls was Labour's shadow chancellor; the wordplay loosely hints at an ower, someone admitting debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow moos, or lows, so a cow is literally something that lows.

clue.text: Sagging pop foursome releases one in hurry

indicators.note: releasing something lets it go, so a single letter is dropped
in places one piece inside another

blocks.note: to fly is to hurry
Abba was a four-member Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: An ageing pop quartet puts out a new release in haste.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft, loose and hanging flesh droops downwards, lacking firmness or tone.

clue.text: Tart offers resistance when collared by a team of cops

indicators.note: being collared means being caught and held, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's detectives
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A prostitute resists arrest when detectives grab her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' wants to be a person of loose morals; it is an adjective meaning sharp-tasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a sharp, sour or bitter taste or smell that stings the mouth or nose.

clue.text: see 14ac.
Front-of-vehicle feature that masks flatulence?

blocks.note: wind is gas in the gut
to screen is to mask or hide

explanation.surface: A car part reimagined as something that hides farts.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the joke: a windscreen screens wind, so it might hide flatulence.
explanation.definitionFit: The glass panel at the front of a car protects the driver from the airflow while driving.

clue.text: Freak rum rots nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild

blocks.note: rum is old slang for strange or peculiar
taken as written

explanation.surface: A weird headline: rum decays nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is a dated British adjective for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A peculiar, eccentric individual who is unusual in behaviour may be called a weirdo or oddball.

clue.text: Rejected Miliband pointer, perhaps, on 'fascist organisation' Nike?

indicators.note: rejected things are sent back, so the words are read backwards

blocks.note: Ed Miliband, the former Labour leader
a pointer is a breed of dog
the SS was the Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A rejected Labour leader's pointer comments on a sportswear brand called fascist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ed Miliband led Britain's Labour Party and lost the 2015 election. Nike looks like the sportswear brand but is the deity it was named after.
explanation.definitionFit: Nike was the Greek deity personifying victory, so she is one example of a female divinity.
